B09.visual_intent: ACT TITLE 'Predict Before You Write' (serif 40, top-left; `walker-claude` in DIM Menlo top-right; tags 'recorded output' and 'instructor example · A. I.-written'). An outline-only terminal frame (Menlo 20, no gutter) holds the REAL output of three read-only commands run in the instructor example's repository, replayed verbatim (evidence/act2/b09-run-git-manim.sh -> b09-git-output-manim.txt, 13 rows, embedded as the literal A2_GIT and asserted equal by evidence/act2/verify_arithmetic.py), the three command lines in DIM ink above their output: `cd assignments/05-shaders-materials`; `git log --reverse --date=short --format='%h %ad' -- CHANGE-BRIEF.md` -> 93be391 2026-10-14 / 48c6177 2026-10-16 (the original brief and a later commit on the same file); `git show --stat --format='%h' 93be391` -> five files, none a shader file, '5 files changed, 85 insertions(+)'. B09.motion_claim: The brief's log lands, then the stat of its commit lands file by file (five files, no shader); after the midpoint the stat is ringed, the original and the dated revision are ringed on 'the original' and 'dated revisions', and the brief's own row on 'this file'.

git show --stat, the five files land
ring on the five-file summary (after the midpoint)

B09.runner_up: Remotion CCPlainShell replaying the same commands with the longer log subjects (kept under 'alt'; it cannot carry the serif act title)
B09.why: The act title must be a serif 40 label top-left (lecture skill), which CCPlainShell cannot draw, so the real git output is replayed in a Manim terminal frame. Real rows are never reflowed and Menlo 20 holds ~80 characters, so the log prints hash and date only and the stat prints the hash only (the CCPlainShell version showed the 98-character subject row). Then `cd assignments/05-shaders-materials` and `git log --reverse --format='%h %ad  %s' --date=format:'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' -- CHANGE-BRIEF.md`: the original commit (93be391, 2026-10-14 00:29) and a later commit on the same file (48c6177, 2026-10-16 00:51), each ringed.
alt.motion_claim: The stat lands as 'before you write either shader' is spoken and its summary line (five files, no shader) is ringed; after the midpoint the log lands: the original brief's commit on 'Keep the original', then the later dated commit on the same file on 'add dated revisions'.

show.event: git show --stat command, then the commit subject
the five files of the brief's commit land
cd + git log command, then the original commit line, ringed
the later commit on the same file lands, ringed

alt.runner_up: Manim: a file icon (the brief) with the original and a dated revision stacked as two commit tags
alt.why: A command that was really run plays as itself (SHOW-THE-THING rung 1): the stat is the proof of 'before any shader' (five files, none a .gdshader), and the log is the proof of 'keep the original, add dated revisions' (two commits on one file, the second 16 Oct). A drawn file icon would only say the same thing without the evidence. Cues are FRAMES at 30 fps for the 9.06 s estimate: when the audio exists re-time them as round(fraction x audio seconds x 30) using the fractions in show[]; none may fall in the 45-55% window (frames 122-149 at the estimate); the largest cue is 184 frames, 68% of the estimate. Line indices count the leading comment line.

B10.visual_intent: Three REAL lab frames of the example's pad, cropped (captures/lab frames 300, 597, 609: scripted input, pad idle 0%, charging 27%, charging 94%; light floor, framed), land on 'what the effect communicates'; the script card lands on 'which script holds it': two real lines of garden.gd with their real numbers (line 4 const CHARGE_SECONDS := 0.6, line 11 var charge := 0.0). On 'the pad shows charge' a grey-backed terracotta ring lands on the 94% frame; on 'one script owns it' a ring lands on the charge line; on 'the shader only watches' the shader card (signal.gdshader) arrives with a drawn eye, an arrow carries charge into it, and an arrow carries it on to the pad. Tags: 'scripted input' (the frames) and 'instructor example · A. I.-written'.
B10.motion_claim: The pad's colour state grows 0% -> 27% -> 94% as the voice says what the effect communicates; the state's owner (a ringed line of garden.gd) feeds the shader card, whose eye watches, and the shader feeds the pad.

show.event: garden.gd card with line 4 and line 11

B10.runner_up: Isometric drawing (show-tell iso kit): a script block, a shader card and a pad tile joined by arrows
B10.why: The pad is shown as the real thing (three real lab frames, not a tile drawing) and the owner as the real two lines of garden.gd; an isometric drawing could only stand in for both. The eye on the shader card says 'watches' with no text sentence.

B11.visual_intent: The specification as a table that fills in column by column on the spoken words. Header row: `shaders/signal.gdshader` (path), `shader_type spatial;` (type, real line 1). Columns name / type / hint / default / set by land on 'each uniform's name', 'type, hint', 'hint, default', 'default, and', 'what sets it'; the four rows are signal.gdshader lines 3-6 read verbatim (activation float hint_range 0.0-1.0 default 0.0; quiet_color vec4 source_color default as a colour chip; active_color vec4 source_color chip; stripe_count float hint_range 1.0-16.0 default 8.0), numbered 3-6. Defaults are drawn from the real lines (a slider with a terracotta dot at the default; two colour chips of the real defaults x 255). 'set by': garden.gd for activation only (garden.gd line 253); 'default' for the other three. '4 uniforms' lands on 'The example has four'; a grey-backed terracotta ring lands on `garden.gd` on 'Only activation'.
B11.motion_claim: Each column of the spec lands on the word that names it; the ring on garden.gd in the 'set by' column lands on 'Only activation comes from the game'.
B11.runner_up: ShowTellCard dashboard: four uniform cards with their five fields each
B11.why: A specification IS a table, and the film's job is to show what a good one holds; the columns landing on their words teach the five fields in order, and drawing the range and default (slider, colour chip) from the real lines carries more than repeating the numbers.

B12.visual_intent: The whole real signal.gdshader (11 lines, Menlo 20, real numbers, real indentation) in an outlined frame; only line 10 shows at first and a terracotta ring lands on it as 'the one line' is said. On 'You write the shader from it' the other ten lines write in around it. Then the line is run as arithmetic: an arrow labelled 'predict' leads to a bar from `base` (the dark-stripe colour, quiet_color x 0.65) to `active_color`, and on 'Here it mixes' a terracotta dot labelled `activation` slides 0 -> 1 along the bar while the `ALBEDO` swatch changes from the base colour to the active colour. Tag: instructor example.
B12.motion_claim: The shader is written around its colour line; then the colour line runs: the activation dot slides along base -> active_color and ALBEDO follows it.

show.event: predict arrow + mix bar + ALBEDO swatch

B12.runner_up: Remotion ClaudeCodeBeat: the file with line 10 ringed and a caption
B12.why: The beat has two claims (the line is the source of the shader; the line is what you predict from). Writing the file in around the ringed line and then running the line as a mix bar carries both with motion; a static ringed listing would read the same as a still.

B13.visual_intent: A RULE, not a measurement (tag 'a rule, not a result'). One ruler of 0.6 s (dimension arrow '0.6 s', garden.gd line 4) with frame ticks at 60 per second; a terracotta dot slides along it with a grey bar filling behind, labelled 0.0 at the start and 1.0 at the end ('the uniform's value at start and end'). On 'the same game time' two more rulers of the same length land, labelled 30 fps (few ticks) and 144 fps (many ticks); after the midpoint all three bars reset and fill together and finish at the same instant ('at thirty, sixty and 144'). On 'A second press' the other two rulers clear, a key cap E with a down arrow presses at the start of the 60 fps ruler and the bar fills in; 'restart', 'extend', 'ignore' list at the right; a second E arrow lands mid-fill and, on 'The example ignores it', is turned away with a cross while the bar goes on; a ring lands on 'ignore' (instructor-example tag).
B13.motion_claim: Three rulers with different tick densities finish filling at the same instant (same game time at any frame rate); a second press is turned away and the bar carries on.

show.event: E press at the start of the 60 fps ruler
second press turned away, ring on ignore

B13.runner_up: Remotion chart: three horizontal bars filling over 0.6 s
B13.why: Tick density is the only way to SEE 'same game time at different frame rates' without quoting a count (0.6 s holds 18, 36 and 86.4 frames, so no count is shown); the second-press picture needs a timeline anyway, so one ruler carries both halves.
B13.sparse_reason: Rulers and bars on cream: the picture is a few long thin objects; the voice carries the explanation.

B14.visual_intent: Phase 1: a fence (outlined box titled 'unchanged') closes round four labels that land on their words: collision, movement, input, earlier tests. Presentation (a box with an eye) lands outside it; an arrow from the fence to presentation is labelled 'reads'; an arrow back toward the fence is labelled 'writes' and is crossed out on 'never writes'. Phase 2: the picture clears and four of the example's own rules land in a stack (timing, reset, colour, readability); on 'a headless test' timing and reset move left under a drawn terminal icon ('headless test'), on 'or your own eyes' colour and readability move right under a drawn eye ('your eyes'). Tag: instructor example.
B14.motion_claim: What must not change is fenced; presentation's arrow only goes in; then each rule is sorted to the terminal or to the eye.

show.event: timing + reset move under the terminal icon
colour + readability move under the eye

B14.runner_up: ShowTellCard focus: a two-column ledger card
B14.why: 'Fence' and 'one-way arrow' are mechanisms a viewer can read with the sound off; the ledger reuses the terminal and eye marks (the act's cast) and takes its four rules from the example's own records (driver-test check names; MATERIALS.md and the brief for what a headless pass cannot certify).
B14.sparse_reason: Phase 1 is a fenced list and one box on cream; phase 2 is two columns; the voice carries the explanation.

B15.visual_intent: Hand arithmetic for ONE pixel, animated, beside the example's prediction table. Right: a 3 x 2 table (activation 0.0 / 0.5 / 1.0; dark and light stripe) of empty slots lands on 'three uniform values, two pixels'. Left, on 'the quiet colour': quiet_color (0.40, 0.16, 0.09) with its swatch; on 'times point six five': a drawn x, 0.65, a rule and (0.26, 0.104, 0.0585); on 'sixty-six, twenty-seven, fifteen': a drawn x, 255, a rule and (66, 27, 15) with its swatch, which flies into the 0.0 / dark slot; then the other five predicted swatches fill with their RGB8 numbers (dark: 66,27,15 / 48,105,74 / 31,184,133; light: 102,41,23 / 66,112,78 / 31,184,133, all from controlled-predictions.json). On 'Only unshaded' real line 2 of signal.gdshader (`render_mode unshaded;`) lands and a ring closes on it. Tags: 'computed by hand, not measured', instructor example.
B15.motion_claim: One pixel is carried through the arithmetic (x 0.65, x 255) and drops into its cell in the prediction table; then the rest of the table fills; then the unshaded line is ringed.
B15.runner_up: ShowTellCard chart: the six predicted values as bars
B15.why: The claim is a calculation: seeing each step land (x 0.65, then x 255) and the result drop into a table is the teaching; the colours are the example's real predictions and the swatches make the three-value, two-pixel plan visible.

B16.visual_intent: A drawing of the assignment's sRGB encode function. Right: two rows of three grey bands (the real 3 x 1 file's values 64 / 128 / 192): row one 'source_color' (dashed legend), row two 'no hint' (solid legend), each band numbered, landing on 'greys sixty-four, one twenty-eight, one ninety-two'; tag 'predicted, not measured'. On 'By the S R G B formula' a plot lands: x = file value, y = on screen, a dashed diagonal (colour read: unchanged) and the encode curve (ink). On 'the colour read alone' three ink dots land on the diagonal; on 'brightens the data read' three terracotta dots rise from the diagonal to the curve with dashed guides, and on each spoken value the y-axis label (137, 188, 225) lands, the matching bottom band brightens to that grey and its number changes (64 -> 137, 128 -> 188, 192 -> 225). On 'On Compatibility' the tag 'Compatibility: measure first' lands. A drawing of predictions, never styled as a capture.
B16.motion_claim: The data read's three points climb from the diagonal to the curve and the bottom row's greys brighten to 137 / 188 / 225 as they are spoken; the colour read stays on the diagonal and its row stays 64 / 128 / 192.

show.event: terracotta dots rise to the curve

B16.runner_up: Remotion chart: the encode curve with three marked points (no bands)
B16.why: The curve shows why 64, 128, 192 move by different amounts and the bands show what the player would see; the diagonal-versus-curve contrast makes 'leaves the colour read alone, brightens the data read' a motion, not a sentence.

B17.visual_intent: Phase 1 (before the midpoint): the example's material plan as a board. The two real textures (ev_tex_color.png, ev_tex_rough.png, framed thumbnails) with their file names (gate-color.png: colour, source_color; gate-roughness.png: data, no hint), the import settings both share (lossless, normal map: disabled, mipmaps: off; compress/mode=0, compress/normal_map=2, mipmaps/generate=false in the .import files) and the uniforms of surface.gdshader in their groups (Surface: tint vec4, roughness_gain float; Pattern: uv_scale float, metallic_gain float). Phase 2 (after 'Predict at least three'): the board clears; three empty panels (dim 'failure' and a dim circle for its check) land, then a fourth on 'The example predicted four'; each fills on its phrase with the example's own prediction and the check that catches it: colour hint (terminal icon: the test), uniform name (terminal icon: the test), shader vs material (eye: the native captures), headless vs colour (eye). Tag: instructor example.
B17.motion_claim: The plan board is replaced by empty failure/check panels (at least three), a fourth lands, and each fills with the example's prediction and its check as the voice names it.
B17.runner_up: Manim: one plain table of the MATERIALS.md rows beside four check marks
B17.why: Two pictures in time (a beat of 16 s): the plan is shown with the real textures and real names, then the empty panels teach the SHAPE of a failure prediction (a failure and its check) before the example fills them. Check icons (terminal, eye) are the act's cast from the evidence split of B14.
B17.sparse_reason: At the midpoint the frame holds three empty outline panels on purpose: the structure (failure, check) is the point of that sentence.

B18.visual_intent: Five numbered circles with one-word labels (renderer, colour, frames, default, clamp?) land on the five questions in the assignment's order, a terracotta dot pointing at the question being spoken. The third question opens a small sum for an ILLUSTRATIVE 36-frame effect (tag 'illustrative: 36 frames'; not the example's): rows '30 fps  36 / 30 = 1.2 s', '60 fps  36 / 60 = 0.6 s', '144 fps  36 / 144 = 0.25 s', each with a grey bar to scale (1.2 s longest), landing on 'frame-counting' and 'three frame rates'.
B18.motion_claim: The same 36-frame effect lasts 1.2 s, 0.6 s and 0.25 s: three bars of different length grow as the three frame rates are named; the pointer walks down the five questions.
B18.why: The five questions are an outline the voice reads; the one that needs a picture is the frame-counting question, and a sum with bars to scale shows the answer's consequence (a frame-counted effect changes with the frame rate) while the numbered dots keep the outline.
B18.sparse_reason: Five short labels and a three-row sum on cream; the voice carries the explanation.
